title: Music Theory Foundations
description: Sound as elements, then intervals, scales, modes, rhythm, and meter. Harmony as a craft waits until these names are honest. Built to support later heavy-music work, not a conservatory recital track.

sourceReferences.title: MIT 21M.051 Fundamentals of Music
sourceReferences.notes: Elements and rhythm/pitch before major/minor, then functional harmony last. Ear and notation travel with the theory.

sourceReferences.title: Berklee Guitar Fundamentals
sourceReferences.notes: Technique and basic harmonic literacy that death-metal construction should assume, not duplicate.

modules.title: Sound as elements
learningObjectives: Name pitch, duration, loudness, and timbre as independent dimensions
Measure an interval as a ratio you can hear beating

modules.title: Pitch collections
learningObjectives: Build a scale from a tonic and a collection of steps
Distinguish mode, key, and pitch set so gravity is not just inventory

modules.title: Rhythm and meter
learningObjectives: Group pulse into meter and subdivide the beat
Displace or stack pulses without changing the written pitch

concepts.name: Pitch, duration, loudness, timbre
concepts.summary: The four things a note can be before it is a theory problem.
objectives: Name pitch, duration, loudness, and timbre as independent dimensions of a sound
Change one dimension without claiming the others moved

concepts.name: Notation as a map
concepts.summary: A staff is a diagram, not the music.
objectives: Treat notation as a map of sound, not as the music itself
Predict what a score leaves out that the ear still has to hear

concepts.name: Staves and clefs
concepts.summary: Where a pitch sits depends on the clef.
objectives: Read a staff and clef as a decision about which pitches sit on the lines
Predict why a bass riff written in treble is a translation, not a different piece

concepts.name: Octave equivalence
concepts.summary: The same letter, a doubling of frequency.
objectives: State octave equivalence as the same pitch class at a 2:1 ratio
Hear two notes an octave apart as the same letter with a register change

concepts.name: Semitones and the chromatic collection
concepts.summary: Twelve named steps in the common tuning.
objectives: Build the chromatic collection from twelve equal semitones
Count the semitones in a written interval instead of guessing from the staff

concepts.name: Intervals and consonance
concepts.summary: Ratios, beating, and why a fifth sits still.
objectives: Measure an interval as a ratio or a semitone count you can hear beating
Distinguish a just fifth from its equal-tempered stand-in

concepts.name: Hearing an interval
concepts.summary: A name that has to survive without the page.
objectives: Identify a sung or played interval without looking at a staff
Predict the beat you hear when two close partials disagree

concepts.name: Scales
concepts.summary: An ordered pitch collection with a tonic.
objectives: Build a scale as a tonic plus a chosen collection of steps
Write the same pitch set starting on a different tonic and say what changed

concepts.name: The major scale
concepts.summary: W-W-H-W-W-W-H as a pattern, not a mood.
objectives: Spell a major scale from WWHWWWH
Hear the major third as the color that is not the minor third

concepts.name: Minor scales
concepts.summary: Natural, harmonic, melodic — three answers to one tonic.
objectives: Distinguish natural, harmonic, and melodic minor by the sixth and seventh
Predict which raised degree a cadence in minor usually wants

concepts.name: Key and tonic
concepts.summary: The pitch everything else is measured from.
objectives: Name a key as a tonic plus a collection that treats that tonic as home
Predict what a piece is doing if the collection stays and the tonic moves

concepts.name: Modes
concepts.summary: Same pitch set, different tonic gravity.
objectives: Treat a mode as a tonic and a hierarchy, not a scale shape
Contrast parallel and relative mode change

concepts.name: Circle of fifths
concepts.summary: Near keys share almost all their pitches.
objectives: Walk the circle of fifths as a map of key signatures and close relations
Predict the next key a fifth away and the accidental that appears

concepts.name: Enharmonic spelling
concepts.summary: F♯ and G♭ are the same key and a different claim.
objectives: Spell the same pitch two ways when the job in the key is different
Predict why G♯ and A♭ lead in different directions

concepts.name: Pentatonic collections
concepts.summary: A reduced set that still implies a tonic.
objectives: Build a pentatonic collection by leaving out the half-steps of a heptatonic scale
Predict why a pentatonic riff has fewer tendency tones

concepts.name: Pulse and rhythm
concepts.summary: When events happen, independent of which pitch.
objectives: Separate pulse from the pattern of attacks that sit on it
Clap a rhythm that is not just the pulse

concepts.name: Silence as rhythm
concepts.summary: A rest is an event.
objectives: Treat silence as a rhythmic event with a duration
Write a rest that is the point of the bar, not an empty leftover

concepts.name: Meter
concepts.summary: A repeating accent pattern you can count.
objectives: Group pulse into a repeating bar with a downbeat
Distinguish simple and compound division of the beat

concepts.name: Beat subdivision
concepts.summary: Twos and threes inside the beat.
objectives: Subdivide a beat into two, three, or four without changing the bar
Notate a triplet against a binary beat

concepts.name: Tempo
concepts.summary: How fast the pulse is, not how busy the surface is.
objectives: State tempo as the speed of the pulse, independent of the written subdivision
Predict why the same figure feels different at half the marking

concepts.name: Ties and dots
concepts.summary: Ways of writing a duration that crosses a beat.
objectives: Extend a duration with a tie or a dot instead of writing a new attack
Read a dotted quarter plus eighth as a long-short pair

concepts.name: Pickup and downbeat
concepts.summary: Starting before the barline.
objectives: Start a phrase before the downbeat without moving the barline
Predict where the ear still hears 'one'

concepts.name: Syncopation
concepts.summary: Accent where the meter did not ask for one.
objectives: Accent a weak part of the bar so the attack fights the meter
Write a syncopation that is still countable

concepts.name: Polyrhythm, first look
concepts.summary: Two subdivisions at once.
objectives: Stack two pulse groupings that share a longer coincidence
Clap 3:2 as three in the time of two
